scenes.title: So Has China Won?
scenes.voiceover: So has China already won? Not so fast. Adjusted for local prices, its economy is already the world's biggest. In plain dollars, America is still ahead. scenes.title: Eighteen Red Thumbprints
scenes.voiceover: Here's the twist. China's reforms didn't really start in Beijing. They started in a starving village called Xiaogang, in late 1978. In the famine years, families there had been forced to go begging. Now eighteen farmers met in secret. They agreed to split their shared land into family plots and keep the extra food they grew. That was illegal. Why would anyone risk prison for a rice field? Because the alternative was starving. So they promised to raise each other's children if any of them went to prison. They sealed the deal with red thumbprints. The next harvest was bigger than anything the village had seen in years.

scenes.title: Coming Back
scenes.voiceover: Party leaders noticed. Deng later praised the idea, but he didn't invent it. The most powerful man in China was backing eighteen peasants. Within a few years, the idea had spread across the country. Today, that scrap of paper sits in the National Museum of China. So a superpower's comeback began with eighteen hungry farmers breaking the law. Remember 1820? Back then, China produced a third of the world's output. Today, it makes close to a third of the world's manufactured goods. China isn't climbing to a new peak. It's climbing back to an old one. Which superpower should we cover next?
